newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia sells seven firms in privatisation drive.
newsitem.headline: Zambia sells seven firms in privatisation drive.

text.p: The Zambian Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said on Monday that it had sold off seven more state-run enterprises under an ambitious programme that has seen the privatisation of more than half the country's parastatal companies in four years.
A ZPA spokesman said the recently-privatised companies included Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines' (ZCCM) units Zamcargo Holding Ltd and Zambia Detonators (Zamdet) Ltd.
The other newly sold firms were Zambia Concrete Ltd, Luangwa Industries Ltd, Zambia National Insurance Brokers Ltd, Zambia State Financing Co Ltd and Zambia Cashew Co.
"Zamcargo is one of the largest clearing and forwarding companies in Zambia, providing air, sea and surface freight services," the spokesman said.
The company was sold to a management buy-out team and Inter-Trek Ltd for $522,500 with $3.365 million pledged in capital expenditure investment over the next three years.

The spokesman said Norway's Dyno Industrier had acquired the government's 70 percent sharehoding in Zamdet. Zambia Concrete was sold to Fraser Fyfe Ltd, a South African firm, and local group Posiedon Construction. The two firms could invest up to $500,000 in capital expenditure at the plant.
Luangwa Industries Ltd, Zambia's sole producer of bicycles, was bought by Tata Zambia Ltd.
Zambia National Insurance Brokers and Zambia State Financing Co had been bought by management buy-out teams.
Zambia Cashew Co had been sold to Western Cashew Industries Ltd, a company owned by local cashew growers.
"The ZPA is pleased with the increased level of participation by loacl companies in the privatisation programme," the spokesman said.
Last month ZPA said 204 of the country's 326 state-run firms had been sold off, while another 34 were ready for privatisation or under negotiation.
